goal: Own milestone M1 (Read-only cockpit) end-to-end per AUTONOMY_BRIEF.md and PLAN.md §12 M1. Scaffold the Tauri v2 + Svelte 5 + TS + Vite + Rust app from scratch and ship a working read-only PR cockpit on a single deliverable branch. PLAN.md is the contract. M1 deliverables, in order of fan-in: (1) Bootstrap (Tauri v2 + Svelte 5 + TS + Vite + SvelteKit static adapter + Rust crate with sqlx/keyring/octocrab/comrak/ammonia/tree-sitter wasm/notify/git2/specta/tokio/tracing/anyhow + Primer CSS + pnpm workspace + GitHub Actions CI on ubuntu+macos); (2) Auth (gh token import + OAuth Device Flow + PAT + multi-account + OS keychain only); (3) Sync engine v1 (tiered focus-aware polling actor + rate-limit budgeter + REST .diff + ETag conditional + /notifications change detector); (4) Two canonical GraphQL queries (PrDetail fat + InboxRefresh thin batched); (5) SQLite migrations covering PLAN.md §4 tables + denormalized read models + FTS5 + content-addressed blob store with zstd patches; (6) IPC + specta-generated types; (7) Svelte 5 frontend (inbox + PR detail + side-by-side + unified diff with custom virtualized line component + tree-sitter wasm Web Worker); (8) Comrak markdown pipeline + ammonia + GitHub post-processors + content-hash render cache; (9) Markdown corpus regression ≤ 2%; (10) Perf benchmark harness enforcing PLAN.md §10 budgets; (11) Token safety (keychain only, never SQLite, never logs). tasks.name: m1-data-layer
tasks.scopedGoal:
Land the SQLite schema + content-addressed blob store + denormalized read models + pre-seeded fixtures so the rest of M1 can read and write from a real local-first store. All schema lives in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/migrations/` as numbered sqlx migrations. Build a `db::` module that owns the SQLite connection pool, runs migrations on boot, exposes typed read APIs for the denormalized views, and exposes typed write APIs the sync engine and IPC layer will consume in later tasks.

Deliverables:
1) Numbered sqlx migrations covering every table in PLAN.md §4: accounts; repos; repo_subscriptions; users; orgs; pull_requests; pr_labels; pr_assignees; pr_reviewers; pr_projects; pr_milestones; commits; pr_commits (junction with order); comments (kind: issue|review|review_thread_reply); review_threads (path/line/side/start_line/start_side + original_* columns); reviews; check_suites; check_runs; check_annotations; pr_files; pr_patches; notifications; worktrees; pending_mutations; id_mappings; sync_cursors (etag column included); rate_limit_buckets; blob_refs. Every viewer-dependent column carries account_id from day one.
2) Denormalized read models as MATERIALIZED VIEW-style tables maintained by triggers OR plain views computed on read — you pick, but justify in `## Notes`: pr_inbox_rows, pr_detail_summary, unread_counts, file_tree_summary. If you implement triggers, include tests that exercise insert/update/delete paths.
3) FTS5 virtual tables on PR title/body, comments, review bodies, filenames, authors with the standard content-table contentless or external-content pattern (you choose; document in DECISIONS.md). Provide rebuild commands.
4) Content-addressed blob store at `<app_data_dir>/blobs/<sha256-prefix-2>/<sha256>`. Provide `BlobStore::put(bytes, kind)` (returns sha256, ref-counts in `blob_refs`), `BlobStore::get(sha256)`, `BlobStore::put_patch(bytes)` (zstd-compressed with a configurable level), `BlobStore::evict_lru(target_bytes)`. Use `zstd` crate. Patch reads transparently decompress.
5) `db::` module: a `Db` struct holding `sqlx::SqlitePool` (WAL mode, `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, `PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL`, `PRAGMA temp_store=MEMORY`). On startup: ensure app data dir, run migrations, vacuum if older than 7 days. Provide typed read APIs the IPC layer will eventually expose: `list_inbox(account_id)`, `pr_detail_summary(pr_id)`, `pr_files(pr_id, head_sha)`, `pr_patch(pr_id, head_sha)`, etc. Provide write helpers the sync engine will use: upsert_repo/user/pr/comment/review_thread/check_suite/check_run/notification/worktree/etc., plus `apply_pending_mutation` / `record_id_mapping` / `update_sync_cursor` (etag-aware) / `update_rate_limit_bucket`. Every write is a transaction.
6) Pre-seeded SQLite fixtures shipped under `apps/desktop/src-tauri/fixtures/`: a SQL script + binary `.db` baked from running migrations + inserting 200 inbox rows across 3 fake repos, 1 active PR with full timeline (≥50 timeline items), ≥5k-line synthesized diff (use a Python or Rust helper script in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/fixtures/build.rs` or similar so it regenerates deterministically), 5 review threads on the active PR, 10 check runs across 2 suites, 200 notification rows. Document the fixture inventory in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/fixtures/README.md`. Ensure `cargo test` boots from this fixture cleanly via a `Db::open_fixture()` helper.
7) Integration tests in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/` (sqlx + tokio): (a) migrations apply cleanly to an empty file; (b) all denormalized read models match a hand-rolled SQL `SELECT` over the base tables for the seeded fixtures; (c) FTS5 search returns expected hits; (d) blob store round-trip and ref-count behaviour; (e) `Db::open_fixture()` loads the inbox in <50 ms cold from disk on a tmpfs (best-effort timing, log the actual number).
8) Update `DECISIONS.md`: how denormalized views are maintained, how blob LRU works, the fixture-build pipeline, any non-obvious schema choices (e.g. how `original_*` thread coords are stored, the comment `kind` enum mapping, how `id_mappings` reconciles temp→server IDs).

Guardrails:
- Do NOT introduce any GitHub API client code, auth code, or rendering code. Sync engine + auth + markdown live in separate downstream workers; only DB primitives.
- Tokens never go into SQLite columns or fixture files. The `accounts` row holds `token_kind` + `scopes` but not the token itself.
- All public DB APIs must be `&self` async; no global mutable state. Errors surface via `anyhow::Result` (with `thiserror` for domain errors at the boundary).
- Maintain `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` green at handoff.
- The branch already exists for this cloud agent; commit and push to it. Do not rename or rebase.

tasks.name: m1-auth-layer
tasks.scopedGoal:
Land the M1 auth layer end-to-end: three auth paths, OS keychain only, multi-account from day one, and a targeted test proving no token strings ever land in SQLite or logs.

Deliverables:
1) `auth::` module in the Rust crate that exposes a `TokenStore` trait backed by the `keyring` crate. One keychain entry per (host, login). Never persist or log raw tokens.
2) Three Tauri commands consumed in M2 but implemented now (no UI yet): `auth_detect_gh_token` (shells out to `gh auth token` + `gh auth status --show-token` with strict parsing; surfaces `{ host, login, scopes, source: "gh" }` for confirmation; on user accept, stores the token in keychain and creates an `accounts` row with `token_kind="gh-cli"` and scopes list), `auth_oauth_device_start` + `auth_oauth_device_poll` (OAuth Device Flow using `gh` CLI's public client_id `Iv1.b507a08c87ecfe98` per DECISIONS.md; emits a one-time code + verification URL + interval; polls `https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token` until token issued, denied, or expired; stores in keychain on success with `token_kind="oauth-device"`), and `auth_pat_save` (validates a PAT against `GET /user`, persists with `token_kind="pat"`). All three flows write to the `accounts` table (login, host, scopes string, token_kind, created_at) but never store the token itself in SQLite.
3) Multi-account: `accounts` is keyed by `(host, login)`. The auth module exposes `auth_list_accounts`, `auth_switch_account`, `auth_remove_account` (also evicts the keychain entry). The frontend will consume these in m1-frontend; for now expose them as Tauri commands with specta annotations so types flow cleanly later.
4) `TokenClient`: a thin reqwest wrapper that fetches the token from keychain per request, never logs Authorization headers (set up `reqwest::header::HeaderMap` with `sensitive(true)`), and rotates via `auth_refresh` for OAuth tokens when the response is 401. This is a building block consumed by m1-api-sync.
5) Targeted integration test in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/token_safety.rs`: simulate the full auth flow with a mock `keyring` backend (use the `keyring::mock` or a small fake), drive each of the three Tauri commands to save a token, drive a synthetic sync (which can be a stub that calls `TokenClient::request` against `https://httpbin.org/headers` or a local mock server), then assert: (a) `SELECT * FROM accounts` contains no column whose value matches the token regex; (b) the SQLite WAL/DB file on disk contains no occurrence of the token bytes; (c) every `tracing` event captured during the run is scrubbed of the token (use `tracing-subscriber` capture layer). The test must fail loud if any of those three checks find the token.
6) `auth::gh::detect_gh_scopes` must be resilient when `gh` is not installed (return a typed `GhMissing` error). When `gh` is installed but the user is not logged in (`gh auth status` exit code != 0), return `GhNotLoggedIn`. The frontend uses these distinctions to render the right next step.
7) Update `DECISIONS.md`: keyring fallback strategy for Linux without Secret Service (per synthesis.md §4 verify-next), document the OAuth Device Flow polling cadence and the exact GH client_id you're using, document the token-safety test approach so future tasks don't regress it.

Guardrails:
- No frontend UI yet; the Svelte side is a separate downstream worker. Just Tauri commands + specta-friendly types.
- Never write tokens to SQLite columns, not even encrypted. Keychain only.
- The token-safety test is non-negotiable; CI must run it.
- `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` green at handoff.
- The cloud-agent branch already exists; commit and push to it.
acceptance: `auth_detect_gh_token`, `auth_oauth_device_start`/`auth_oauth_device_poll`, and `auth_pat_save` exist as Tauri commands and are listed in the `auth::` module API.
All three paths land tokens only in the OS keychain via the `keyring` crate.
`accounts` table is populated with `(host, login, token_kind, scopes, created_at)` and is the source of truth for the account list.
Multi-account: at least two distinct `(host, login)` entries can coexist; `auth_switch_account` flips the active account without mutating tokens.
`apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/token_safety.rs` proves no token strings appear in SQLite, the DB file on disk, or `tracing` log output across the full auth + dummy-sync cycle.
`cargo test --workspace` and `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` are green.
DECISIONS.md updated with auth-specific choices.

tasks.name: m1-api-sync
tasks.scopedGoal:
Build the GitHub API client + sync engine v1 end-to-end so the SQLite cache populates from real (or mocked) GitHub data. Two canonical hand-written GraphQL queries; tiered focus-aware polling actor; rate-limit budgeter; REST `.diff` fetch with `Accept: application/vnd.github.v3.diff`; conditional ETag/If-None-Match path; `/notifications` change-detector honoring `If-Modified-Since` + `X-Poll-Interval`; `mergeable: null` backoff.

Deliverables:
1) `api::` module: a `GithubClient` consuming `auth::TokenClient` from m1-auth-layer. Two transports: REST (reqwest, JSON + diff response handlers) and GraphQL (one fat POST endpoint). Either octocrab as a wrapper or a hand-rolled reqwest client — you pick; document in DECISIONS.md.
2) Two canonical hand-written GraphQL queries under `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/api/queries/`:
   - `PrDetail.graphql`: one fat query covering title, body, timeline items (paged), review threads, reviews, check suite summary, labels, assignees, requested reviewers, mergeable, headRef + baseRef + headRepository. Includes a `revision` const documenting the schema version we're targeting.
   - `InboxRefresh.graphql`: thin batched query taking `[ID!]!` (up to 20) and returning only the fields `pr_inbox_rows` renders (number, title, updatedAt, author, isDraft, state, mergeable state, labels, requested reviewers, check summary roll-up, unread bool placeholder).
   No per-component GraphQL elsewhere. Add a clippy lint or a `tests/canonical_queries.rs` test that scans `apps/desktop/**` for stray `gql!` or `.graphql` files outside this directory and fails if any are found.
3) `sync::` module:
   - **Tiered focus-aware polling actor** per PLAN.md §2.1. Spawn `tokio` tasks for Hot/Warm/Cool/Cold tiers with the listed cadences (focused vs background); pause every tier 5 min after window unfocus (use a `FocusState` signal channel; default to focused; m1-frontend will wire window events later).
   - **Rate-limit budgeter** actor: parses `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`, `X-RateLimit-Used` headers; maintains a `rate_limit_buckets` row per (account, resource: graphql|core). Throttles background tasks when GraphQL points < 1000 or REST < 500. Foreground (user-initiated) calls bypass back-pressure via a `Priority::Foreground` lane.
   - **REST .diff** path: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}` with `Accept: application/vnd.github.v3.diff`; stores raw diff text into the blob store via `BlobStore::put_patch` (zstd-compressed); writes `pr_patches(pr_id, head_sha, patch_blob_sha)`.
   - **Conditional ETag/If-None-Match**: every REST call writes its `ETag` to `sync_cursors.etag` and replays it on the next request; 304 short-circuits without bumping rate limit.
   - **/notifications change detector**: `GET /notifications since=<last_modified> participating=false` with `If-Modified-Since` honoring `Last-Modified`, respect `X-Poll-Interval` for cadence floor. On a non-304, fan out targeted GraphQL refetches via a `RefetchScheduler` channel.
   - **`mergeable: null` backoff**: a dedicated re-poll task with schedule 2s, 5s, 15s, 45s, 2min, max 5min per PR.
   - **TierActions trait** per existing DECISIONS.md entry: scheduler calls a `dyn TierActions` injected at construction (production wires `Arc<RealActions>`; tests inject counts/stubs).
4) Reconciliation: every API response upserts canonical fields into SQLite via the m1-data-layer writers; never invent local IDs; populate `id_mappings` only when a write call from m1-... mutation engine returns server IDs (out of scope for M1 but the table is ready).
5) Mock/online split: under `cfg(test)` and in `tests/`, use `wiremock` (or `mockito`) to stand up GitHub-shaped responses including ETag + 304, rate-limit headers, and `mergeable: null` recovery. Provide one optional integration test under `tests/online_demo.rs` gated on `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var: hit `theolundqvist/pr-cockpit-v2` (public repo created for this) for an inbox refresh; the test no-ops cleanly when the token is absent so CI doesn't block.
6) Integration tests (must run offline by default):
   - Tiered scheduler: focused vs background cadence drift, 5-min unfocus pause, foreground bypass.
   - Rate-limit budgeter: drops below threshold → background lane throttled, foreground lane untouched.
   - ETag 304 path: second call with `If-None-Match` matching the stored etag returns 304, no DB write happens, counter doesn't decrement.
   - `mergeable: null` recovery: backoff schedule observed precisely (drive a virtual clock; the actor must accept a `Clock` trait for testability).
   - PrDetail upsert: feeding a recorded GraphQL response yields the expected SQLite rows in `pull_requests`, `comments`, `review_threads`, `reviews`, `check_*`, `pr_labels`, `pr_assignees`, `pr_reviewers`.
7) Update `DECISIONS.md`: octocrab vs hand-rolled client choice with reasoning, GraphQL schema revision pinning, refetch fanout ordering, and the virtual `Clock` trait for testability.

Guardrails:
- No frontend code in this task. The IPC layer is a separate downstream worker. Expose `sync::start` and `sync::shutdown` from `lib.rs`.
- Never log Authorization headers (`reqwest::header::sensitive`).
- All public APIs are `async fn` returning `anyhow::Result`.

tasks.name: m1-markdown-pipeline
tasks.scopedGoal:
Land the canonical markdown render pipeline in Rust and its CI-enforced fidelity corpus.

Deliverables:
1) `render::` module: `render_comment(body: &str, ctx: &RenderCtx) -> RenderedHtml`. Pipeline = comrak (cmark-gfm-compatible: tables, task lists, footnotes, strikethrough, autolinks, math, alerts where supported) → GitHub-specific post-processors → ammonia sanitization. Post-processors must handle: GitHub alert blocks (`> [!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]`, `[!CAUTION]`), suggestion fences (\`\`\`suggestion ... \`\`\`), `@user` autolinks (link to `https://github.com/<user>`), `#123` issue/PR autolinks (link to `https://github.com/<repo>/issues/123` resolved against `ctx.repo`), SHA autolinks (7–40 hex, link to `https://github.com/<repo>/commit/<sha>`), emoji shortcodes (`:rocket:` → SVG-via-octicons fallback or the Unicode equivalent — pick one; document the choice).
2) Content-hash render cache: every render is keyed by `(sha256(body), renderer_version)`. The cache lives in `blob_refs` with `kind="rendered-html"`; cached HTML lives in the blob store. `RENDERER_VERSION` is a `&'static str` exposed in `lib.rs` and bumped any time the pipeline changes shape. Cache hits skip the whole pipeline.
3) Sanitization sits at the boundary via ammonia. Allow GitHub-shaped HTML (tables, task list checkboxes, code blocks with `data-language` attributes, alert blockquotes, suggestion `<div class="suggestion-block">`, autolinks with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`). Strip every script/style/iframe/object/embed/javascript:.
4) Markdown corpus regression harness under `tools/markdown-corpus/`:
   - `corpus.json`: a list of ~200 real PR-comment bodies. Source = public-repo comment bodies fetched via the GitHub REST API (when `GITHUB_TOKEN` is set in CI you may re-fetch; otherwise reuse the committed snapshot). Each entry: `{ id, source_url, body, oracle_html_sha, repo? }`.
   - `fetch.ts` (Node, vitest-runnable): one-time refresh script that uses GitHub's API to pull 200 representative comment bodies across `cli/cli`, `microsoft/vscode`, `rust-lang/rust`, `kubernetes/kubernetes` (or similar) covering tables, task lists, alerts, suggestion fences, math, mentions, autolinks. Commit the snapshot + checked-in `oracle.html` per entry, where `oracle.html` is the GitHub `POST /markdown` REST endpoint's output (or `POST /repos/.../markdown` when context is needed). Document the fetch command + how to refresh in `tools/markdown-corpus/README.md`.
   - `score.ts` / `score.rs`: text-diff metric. Compute structural diff = normalized DOM-trees (drop whitespace, sort class lists, drop GitHub-specific anchor URLs that the harness can't reproduce). Compute pixel-equivalent: render both `oracle.html` and `cockpit.html` through `jsdom` (or `linkedom`) into the same shadow root, take a string-level diff weighted by visible-character mismatches over total characters, output a fraction. The CI gate is ≤2%.
   - `pnpm corpus` runs the harness end-to-end and exits non-zero on the gate. Hooks into the existing `markdown-corpus` CI job.
5) Tests in `apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/render.rs` covering each post-processor independently (alerts, suggestion fences, @user, #123, SHA, emoji), plus an end-to-end snapshot test against a 10-entry mini-corpus included verbatim in the test (smoke-bound version of the big corpus).
6) Update `DECISIONS.md`: `RENDERER_VERSION` bumping policy, ammonia allowlist rationale, emoji rendering choice, the corpus refresh procedure, why 2% is the right ceiling for M1 (down to 1% at M6).

Guardrails:
- No textarea UI in this task. The composer is a downstream worker.
- All HTML must round-trip through ammonia before leaving Rust. No raw HTML escape hatch.
- The corpus is a snapshot; the M1 CI runs against the snapshot. Online refresh is opt-in via `GITHUB_TOKEN` and never gates CI.
- `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`, and `pnpm corpus` green at handoff.
- The cloud-agent branch already exists; commit and push to it.

tasks.name: m1-frontend
tasks.scopedGoal:
Build the Svelte 5 read-only PR cockpit UI on the generated IPC bindings + Primer CSS. Inbox served from `pr_inbox_rows`; PR detail with description, timeline, labels, reviewers, checks; side-by-side + unified diff viewer with virtualization and tree-sitter wasm highlighting.

Deliverables:
1) `apps/desktop/src/`: SvelteKit static-adapter app. Layout: left sidebar (account switcher + repo subscriptions list + status bar with rate-limit meter), main pane (inbox ↔ PR detail), top bar (search placeholder, focus toggle for the polling actor). Use `@primer/css` classes + `@primer/octicons` SVGs directly. Stick to GitHub's visual cadence.
2) **Inbox** (`/`): served from `pr_inbox_rows` via the `db_list_inbox` IPC command. Render synchronously on cold start from the cached payload baked into `window.__INBOX_SEED__` at app boot (Rust side reads the inbox once before the webview attaches and exposes the data via Tauri's `with_window_state` plugin or an initial `init_inbox` IPC). Row: title, number, repo, author, age, labels, requested-review chip, draft chip, check rollup, unread dot. Click → navigate to `/pr/<id>` with a preload hook that fires `pr_detail_preload(id)` to warm the cache before the route's `load()` resolves.
3) **PR detail** (`/pr/[id]`): three tabs (Conversation, Files, Checks) per github.com. Conversation tab renders the timeline (issue comments, review comments grouped by thread, reviews, label/assignee/state events) using the comrak-rendered HTML payloads from `render_comment_html(body)` IPC. Header shows title, state, draft/ready badge, mergeable badge, base ← head ref, labels chip row, assignees, requested reviewers, milestone, project chips, and a check-summary inline pill. Right rail mirrors github.com (Reviewers / Assignees / Labels / Projects / Milestones / Linked issues placeholder).
4) **Diff viewer**: a custom virtualized line component on `@tanstack/svelte-virtual`. Both unified and side-by-side modes via a toggle. Pulls `pr_patch` (blob-stored zstd diff) via IPC, parses it client-side into a typed structure (`File[] → Hunk[] → Line[]`), virtualizes per hunk. Per-line review thread anchoring uses GitHub's `line`/`side`/`start_line`/`start_side` verbatim from the IPC payload — never compute anchors locally. Show outdated threads collapsed with the server's `isOutdated` badge.
5) **Syntax highlighting**: tree-sitter wasm in a Web Worker (`apps/desktop/src/lib/workers/highlight.ts`). Lazy by viewport: when a line scrolls into view, the worker tokenizes the surrounding window. Hard cap: skip files >5000 lines unless the user clicks "Highlight anyway". Token cache keyed by `(language, content_hash)` in `window.indexedDB`. Grammars served from the vendored grammars dir set up in m1-bootstrap.
6) Live data: every PR detail page subscribes to the matching `pr:<id> changed` Tauri event and re-queries the IPC commands incrementally. The status bar subscribes to `rate_limit:account:<id> changed` and renders the per-account rate-limit budget.
7) Multi-account: account switcher reads `auth_list_accounts`. When an account is active, every command call is implicitly scoped to it (the Rust IPC commands take an `account_id` arg — the frontend supplies it from a stored `$state` value).
8) UX polish: focus rings on every interactive element; full keyboard navigation for the inbox (j/k, Enter); skeletons for cold cache hits (so the <50 ms preloaded budget can still show feedback if the cache is empty); empty-state pages with Primer-styled illustrations from `@primer/octicons`.
9) Frontend tests: `vitest` unit tests for the diff parser, the timeline reducer, the inbox row component, and the Web Worker tokenizer adapter. `playwright` smoke test wiring the offline-fixtures Tauri build: load the inbox, click a PR, open the diff, toggle side-by-side, scroll to the bottom of a 5k-line file. The Playwright smoke can run headless against `pnpm --filter desktop preview`; if the Tauri-bundled binary requires display server in CI, gate it behind `xvfb-run`.
10) Update `DECISIONS.md`: how the inbox cold paint stays <100 ms (initial payload baked into the bundle entrypoint), tree-sitter grammar provisioning at runtime, IndexedDB token cache layout, and the keyboard layer.

Guardrails:
- No SQLite, no direct GitHub API calls in `apps/desktop/src/**`. All IPC via the generated bindings.

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm svelte-check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test` (frontend), `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` green at handoff.
